PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fetch MCP OAuth metadata outside renderer
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #340533

Routes MCP authorization-server metadata discovery through the shared process on desktop instead of renderer `fetch`. This allows OAuth providers whose well-known metadata endpoints do not permit CORS requests to start authentication. Web continues to use the request-service implementation.

Adds regression coverage for an Avalara-style provider where the OAuth metadata endpoint returns 404 and OpenID discovery succeeds.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostAuth.test.ts` — 78 tests passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostMcpOAuthMetadataService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/electron-browser/agentHostMcpOAuthMetadataService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostAuth.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostAuth.test.ts src/vs/code/electron-utility/sharedProcess/sharedProcessMain.ts src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts src/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.ts src/vs/sessions/sessions.common.main.ts src/vs/sessions/sessions.desktop.main.ts` — passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- Live Code OSS test with Avalara ELR — Authenticate opened the Avalara browser login/authorization flow; no metadata CORS failure remained in renderer logs

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop automatic MCP authentication when an agent-host server reports AuthRequired
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider lookup and, only when no matching active/persisted provider exists, OAuth metadata discovery must complete before session lookup and token forwarding can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ProxyChannel call from the desktop renderer to AgentHostMcpOAuthMetadataService in the shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC round trip per authorization server that actually requires metadata; zero for an already active provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The renderer invoked the same discovery helper directly, with no IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC round trip is on the provider-creation critical path, but its payload is only the parsed metadata and discovery URL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET OAuth/OpenID well-known metadata through the shared-process request service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful request when the first discovery endpoint works, otherwise up to three sequential discovery endpoints; the request service can retry transient GET transport failures up to three attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same helper issued one to three sequential renderer fetches. The diff changes transport and adds bounded request-service transient retries, but does not increase normal successful endpoint cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery must finish before a dynamic provider can be created; subsequent active-provider authentication skips it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authorization-server count in one protected-resource challenge; servers are processed sequentially, and each uncached server can probe up to three well-known URLs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authorization servers within one challenge are sequential. SequencerByKey serializes creation for the same dynamic provider; distinct providers may proceed concurrently. Session-handler pending operations coalesce identical in-flight attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An active or persisted matching authentication provider bypasses metadata discovery. The new service adds no metadata cache, but this matches the pre-diff discovery lifecycle; failures can be retried by later auth events. Transport HTTP caching remains available.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the provider checks, keyed sequencer, call path, IPC proxy, discovery loop, and request retry policy are directly visible in the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Shared-process IPC and transient retry overhead vary by machine and network, but normal successful discovery adds only one small IPC exchange and retains the same network cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added IPC is bounded and necessary to remove CORS from desktop discovery; normal network fan-out is unchanged, while extra retries occur only on bounded transient-failure paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive desktop MCP sign-in from server customization UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Starting the server, resolving or creating the provider, fetching metadata when needed, and session creation are all on the user-triggered sign-in path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Desktop metadata service invocation in the shared process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one IPC call per authorization server reached and needing provider creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Metadata discovery ran directly in the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a small IPC hop before the network request on first provider creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One to three sequential discovery URLs per reached uncached authorization server, with bounded retries only for transient transport errors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The renderer used the same one-to-three-URL discovery helper; only the transport location changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of authorization servers advertised by the selected MCP server; iteration stops at the first successful authentication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Authorization servers are tried serially, and same-provider creation is serialized by SequencerByKey. Different user-triggered providers can overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing/activated providers and matching stored client registrations avoid metadata fetches. There is no new long-lived retained metadata state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the customization call site and provider-creation path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact metadata endpoint latency and frequency of transient transport errors are provider-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The behavior remains demand-driven, serial per challenge, and bounded; no new collection-wide fan-out, retained cache, or unbounded allocation is introduced.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: When provider metadata is absent, the delayed common service delegates discovery to IRequestService before provider creation. In browser deployments, a failed/405 browser request may fall back to the remote request channel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser request for each OAuth/OpenID discovery endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one request for first-endpoint success, up to three sequential endpoints on misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct fetch used the same discovery endpoint sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for first provider creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: BrowserRequestService fallback through the remote-agent request channel after browser failure or status 405 when a remote connection exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one remote fallback per attempted discovery endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct global fetch had no remote fallback and the authentication attempt failed after its browser-side discovery probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Allows discovery to continue after a browser-side failure instead of terminating unsuccessfully.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authorization-server count and the same maximum of three discovery endpoint variants per server.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same keyed provider serialization and sequential authorization-server traversal as desktop; distinct provider keys may overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider activation/registration remains the effective warm cache. The service itself is delayed and does not retain responses.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the service and fallback call paths; provider-specific endpoint behavior is variable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote fallback prevalence depends on deployment, CORS policy, and remote connection presence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The additional remote boundary occurs only to turn a previously failed discovery into a progressing authentication flow and remains bounded by the existing discovery sequence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench and shared-process startup without MCP authentication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module registration occurs during startup, but renderer-side services are delayed; shared-process channel setup constructs only the thin metadata service around an already-created request service and performs no request.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per process/window, independent of MCP server or workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No authentication work or network operation is scheduled at startup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No metadata, response body, or per-server state is allocated until fetch is invoked.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructors and registration descriptors are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Object construction cost is negligible and contains no transitive I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No eager-work regression: no network, filesystem, subprocess, or IPC call is initiated merely by registration.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all nine changed files and traced desktop, web/Sessions, automatic, interactive, and startup paths. The PR moves first-use metadata discovery behind a bounded IPC service on desktop and through the existing request service elsewhere, without increasing normal successful network fan-out, introducing unbounded retention, or adding eager expensive startup work. No high-confidence actionable performance regression found.
